properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-12, after watching "near miss" and small repeated slips across the whole development: *"if they are reoccurring little issues, the agent should capture them in its own notes so that it can learn from its past mistakes … notes in the governance/management nodes, strictly to speak past agent to present agent … little oddities like how to properly do tag and release, little issues that continue to bite us in GitHub, or guard issues."* His own counter: *"Claude already has its own Memory.md/Claude.md, which I feel already serves similar purposes."* His scope: *"this isn't just for reflow2 — for anybody that uses reflow2 on their own design project using any agent/model; specific about passing design details from past agent to present agent across sessions."* His final question: *"would an agent even use it, or would it be helpful for the agent to have its own notepad?"*

═══ WHAT WAS FOUND BY LOOKING, 2026-09-12 ═══

① THE NOTEPAD ALREADY EXISTS, AND HE ALREADY RULED ON THE MEMORY-FILE HALF. `rule:a-rule-the-project-follows-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-an-agents-memory` (his word, 2026-09-04): a habit, convention, trap or way of doing a step goes in the graph as a DesignRule, Decision or TemporalFact hung off the node it concerns; the memory file holds a pointer, never the content. Reason: memory is machine-local and harness-local; the graph travels with the repo and is the only place that can ACT on a rule. The Memory.md go-back is therefore already answered, by him.

② THE RULE IS BEING BROKEN AS THIS IS WRITTEN. The agent's memory file on this machine holds roughly ten "little oddities" of exactly the kind he describes and none of them is in the graph: `gh pr checks --json` is unsupported and reads as a false all-clear; `gh pr edit` fails on a Projects-classic GraphQL error and changes nothing (REST PATCH works); `plan_epoch` on an existing epoch resets its status to `planned`; a shell chain `gate | tail -1 && git commit` commits on a red gate; `--stop-shared` then any tool call refreshes a stale daemon before an export; `pkill -f` on a pattern matching your own shell kills it. Every one is portable to another machine and another agent, and today none of them travel.

③ THE MEASURED ANSWER TO "WOULD AN AGENT USE IT" IS: NOT BY READING. `fact:the-gate-caught-the-agent-six-times-and-five-were-the-same-two-habits` (2026-08-26): the agent wrote the lesson out in prose and made the same shell construction twenty minutes later — *"a lesson recorded in conversation does not change the next command; a gate does."* `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` sits in the graph AND in memory and was still broken five ways on 2026-09-04. And today (2026-09-12) the `| tail` pipe committed on a red gate again — a trap first recorded on 2026-08-14 as `fact:a-piped-gate-reports-the-pipes-exit-code-not-the-gates`. The same lesson has now been written three times in three places and repeated anyway. What DID stop each recurrence was a check at the step: the intent-authority gate, the lineage gate, the duplicate guard, and today `toolsnap.py --update` refusing to bless a bad surface.

④ THE PRIOR BRAINSTORM ON THIS FOUND THE GAP IS A VIEW, NOT CAPTURE. `dec:idea-where-do-lessons-learned-live-and-can-a-user-state-a-precondition` (2026-08-30): the release lessons ARE in the graph, scattered across DesignRule, Flow and TemporalFact, with no single home and no single view — which node type a lesson lands in depends on the session that wrote it.

═══ THE IDEAS, WITH THEIR COSTS AND HONEST COUNTERS ═══

A. A NOTEPAD NODE TYPE (`Note` / `Lesson`), or a `note_kind: agent` on Fragment. Cheap to add; his instinct. COUNTER: a vocabulary distinction has to be READ by some computation to earn its place (the bar `Decision.kind` cleared), and nothing would read a Note that does not already read a DesignRule or TemporalFact. It would be a fourth home for a lesson when the finding in ④ is that three is already too many. Over-engineering by his own measure.

B. NO NEW TYPE — ONE VIEW. A `lessons` report / `find_tools`-style query that gathers every DesignRule, TemporalFact and Decision carrying a lesson, so a session can read "what has bitten this project" in one call. Closes ④'s gap. COUNTER: ③ says a page of lessons read at session start does not change the command typed an hour later. Necessary for a human; insufficient for an agent.

C. ⭐ A LESSON IS SERVED AT THE STEP IT CONCERNS. The lesson is hung off the node it is about (the Flow step, the Capability, the tool) — the rule already says so — and the served surface DELIVERS it at the moment of use: `get_skill("release")` returns the lessons hung on `flow:release-cut`; a tool whose description or refusal carries the trap ("`| tail` returns the pipe's exit code"); `get_instructions` carrying the project's own enforced rules. This is what reflow2 already does for its tool descriptions ("MEASURED: the export was early in 91 of 200 trials") and it is the one form of note that reaches the agent with its hands on the step. Works for any project, because the hook is the served skill, not a file in a harness. COUNTER: only helps for steps that go through reflow2; a GitHub or shell oddity has no reflow2 step to hang on unless the project models its release flow (reflow2 does: `flow:release-cut`).

D. THE STRONGEST LESSONS BECOME CHECKS — `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` step ②. Measured to be the only thing that stopped a recurrence. COUNTER: not every oddity can be a check (an external CLI's broken subcommand cannot be gated locally); D covers the severe ones, C the rest.

E. HIS "SPEAK PAST AGENT TO PRESENT AGENT" AS A DISTINCT AUDIENCE. Today a lesson node is written for anybody. A note whose audience is explicitly the next agent could be terser and more operational ("do X, not Y, because Z bit us on <date>"). COUNTER: `req:agent-authored-feedback-is-reproducible-and-never-leaves-unasked` already says agent-to-agent text is written for reproduction, and a note nobody but agents read is the memory-file failure with a different file name — his ① reason again. An audience field is cheap; whether it changes anything is unmeasured.

═══ WHERE THIS LEANS (a finding, not a decision) ═══

Not A. The notepad exists; a fourth home makes ④ worse. The working answer is B + C + D together: one view for the human (B), delivery at the step for the agent (C), and a check for anything that has bitten twice (D). The immediate, cheap act is to honour ① — move the ten oddities out of the memory file and into the graph, each hung on the node it concerns — and then measure whether C's delivery is what finally stops a repeat, since the graph now has three recorded recurrences to compare against.
properties.name: SETTLED — promoted into: A lesson a design holds is delivered at the step it concerns — when the skill is fetched or the tool is about to be used — not only where it was filed
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill while PR #489 (increment 434) is in CI; nothing built. Recorded separately from the 2026-08-30 lessons-learned idea because it adds two questions that one did not ask: whether the audience of a lesson is the next AGENT specifically, and whether an agent would read a notepad at all — which the graph turns out to be able to answer with three measured recurrences.
